---
title: "Getting Started"
---

## Installation

### Rust (as a library)

Add the `gridwell` crate to your `Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
gridwell = "0.1"
# or only the formats you need:
# gridwell = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["html", "latex"] }
```

Each format is a [cargo feature](../api/rust.qmd#features), all on by default.

### Python

```bash
pip install gridwell          # Python 3.10+
pip install 'gridwell[gt]'    # include the Great Tables integration
```

### R

```r
# From a source package (needs Rust 1.85 or later):
install.packages("gridwell_0.1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

The source package carries the Rust crates it needs, so it builds offline. In a
checkout of the repository, make it with `cargo xtask r-source` and then
`R CMD build target/r-source/gridwell`.

### CLI Tool

```bash
cargo install gridwell-cli
```

Or build from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rich-iannone/gridwell.git
cd gridwell
cargo build --release -p gridwell-cli
# Binary at: target/release/gridwell
```

## First Table

Create a minimal table IR file called `hello.json`:

```{.json filename="hello.json"}
{
  "ir_version": "1.0",
  "config": {
    "table_cols": 2,
    "header_rows": 1,
    "body_rows": 2,
    "stub_cols": 0,
    "row_striping": false,
    "row_striping_include_stub": false,
    "row_striping_include_body": false,
    "column_labels_hidden": false,
    "locale": "en-US",
    "page_break_mode": "avoid"
  },
  "styles": { "defs": {}, "compositions": {}, "conditionals": [] },
  "header": null,
  "column_spec": [
    { "id": "col_0", "align": "left", "width": "auto", "hidden": false, "label": "Name" },
    { "id": "col_1", "align": "right", "width": "auto", "hidden": false, "label": "Score" }
  ],
  "table": {
    "thead": {
      "rows": [{
        "role": "column_label",
        "cells": [
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "Name"}], "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "scope": "col" },
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "Score"}], "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "scope": "col" }
        ]
      }]
    },
    "tbody": [{
      "rows": [
        { "cells": [
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "Alice"}], "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "data_type": "string" },
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "95"}], "typed_value": {"type": "number", "value": 95}, "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "data_type": "number" }
        ]},
        { "cells": [
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "Bob"}], "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "data_type": "string" },
          { "content": [{"type": "text", "value": "87"}], "typed_value": {"type": "number", "value": 87}, "colspan": 1, "rowspan": 1, "is_stub": false, "is_placeholder": false, "data_type": "number" }
        ]}
      ],
      "summary_rows": []
    }]
  },
  "footer": { "footnotes": [], "source_notes": [] }
}
```

Then render it:

```bash
gridwell convert hello.json --to html
gridwell convert hello.json --to latex
gridwell convert hello.json --to docx -o hello.docx
```

## Using with Great Tables (Python)

```python
from great_tables import GT, exibble
import gridwell

table = gridwell.Table(GT(exibble.head(3)))
html = table.render_html()
table  # in a notebook: the table itself; print(table) draws it as text
```

`gridwell.Table()` also takes IR as a JSON string or a dict.

## Using with gt (R)

```r
library(gt)
library(gridwell)

gt_tbl <- gt(exibble[1:3, ], rowname_col = "row", groupname_col = "group")
html <- gw_render_html(gt_tbl)      # every function takes a gt table
tbl <- as_gw_table(gt_tbl)          # or convert it once
tbl                                 # prints the table drawn as text
```

Every function also takes IR as a JSON string, or a `gw_table` from `gw_parse_ir()`.
In R Markdown and Quarto, a `gw_table` a chunk returns is shown in the document's own
format: HTML, LaTeX (PDF) or Typst.
